paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: God doesn't just do mighty things, He wants His people to REMEMBER them. Israel had just walked across a river on dry ground, and the LORD's next move was to say, 'Grab some stones.' Joshua tells them the stones will be "a memorial to the Israelites forever" (Joshua 4:7). I can't keep track of where I put my own apron, so a pile of rocks sounds like a great plan to me.

Now look at who the stones are for. Joshua says that when their children ask what the stones mean, the fathers are to answer, "Israel crossed the Jordan on dry ground" (Joshua 4:22). So the memory isn't meant to sit in one head. It's meant to get handed down, one answer at a time. And Joshua gives the reason: "so that all the peoples of the earth may know that the hand of the LORD is mighty, and so that you may always fear the LORD your God" (Joshua 4:24).

So what does that mean for you, baker? Think about what God has done in your life, and don't let it fade. Say it out loud, write it down, tell somebody who asks. When the kings heard what happened, "their hearts melted" (Joshua 5:1), and I think that tells us His mighty hand is worth remembering. Set your own stones, friend, and keep telling the story.
